title: A conditional is equivalent to its contrapositive
statement: For all propositions p and q, (p implies q) is equivalent to ((not q) implies (not p)).

evidence.supports: For all propositions p and q, (p implies q) is equivalent to ((not q) implies (not p)).

notes:
The equivalence that makes 'prove the contrapositive instead' a legitimate proof move. Contrast F:affirming-the-consequent, which is the same shape with the negations dropped and is refuted: the two facts together are what distinguishes the contrapositive from the converse, and storing them side by side is more informative than either alone.

On the axiom footprint: it names the trust base of the SMT ROUTE that established this fact -- the axeyum-ir Boolean evaluator, and the two-valued semantics of the SMT-LIB Bool sort that makes exhaustive truth-table enumeration a proof. It is deliberately NOT empty and deliberately NOT a Lean axiom list. Nothing here went through axeyum's Lean kernel. Measured 2026-08-14 with `cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_axiom_inventory`: the `logic` prelude reports axiom=0 opaque=0 quotient=0, and its declarations are exactly True, False, And, Or, Iff, Not (as `a -> False`), Eq and Exists -- an intuitionistic core with no `Classical.em`, no `propext` and no `Quot.sound`. Zero trusted declarations there means the kernel assumes nothing, not that it can prove everything.
